_about: Heat-exchanger networks of the reference brewery (Padullés et al., 2026). Segments: [stream, T_from_C, T_to_C] in the stream's direction. Indirect matches pass through the stratified HR tank.

N0 existing.description: Existing network: the 'common heat recovery solutions' of Padullés et al. (2026), Sec. 4.2, Figs. 5-7: Pfaduko (direct) and wort-cooling heat recovery into a stratified hot-water tank (indirect). Hot utility 11.3 kWh/hl (published, Sec. 4.3.2 and 7).

provenance.tank serves pre-mashing, lautering and C: assumed: Fig. 7 lists pre-mashing, mashing, lautering and CIP; the stratified tank lets heat be reassigned, so the split only affects bookkeeping, not utilities
provenance.extra_dT_K 4 for the tank: published convention: extra 2 K shift per stream for indirect transfer (Sec. 4.1)
provenance.wort end 23 °C: derived: 100 - 7.7 / 0.1 kWh/hl K; equals the lowest end temperature allowed by the 8 K indirect approach to 15 °C water

matches.name: Pfaduko (kettle vapour condenser)
matches.note: Fig. 5: 2.4 kWh/hl from the boil-off to the wort; wort 75 -> 95 °C (derived: 2.4 / 0.12 kWh/hl K); 0.6 kWh/hl external heating 95 -> 100 °C

matches.name: Wort cooling heat recovery (HR tank)
matches.note: Fig. 6: 7.7 kWh/hl from wort cooling (100 -> 23 °C) to the tank

N1 condensate into tank.description: Retrofit 1: condensate from the Pfaduko (boil-off condensate cooling) also charges the HR tank, as Padullés et al. (2026, Sec. 4.2.2) suggest ('recover the leftover stream ... 0.9 kWh/hl').

provenance.condensate into the tank: published suggestion (Sec. 4.2.2); end temperature 23 °C from the same 8 K indirect approach
